question.text: The locus of the mid-points of the chords of an ellipse $x^{2}+4 y^{2}=4$ that are drawn from the positive end of the minor axis, is

options.text: a circle with centre $\left(\frac{1}{2}, 0\right)$ and radius 1
a parabola with focus $\left(\frac{1}{2}, 0\right)$ and directrix $x=-1$
an ellipse with centre $\left(0, \frac{1}{2}\right),$ major axis 1 and minor axis $\frac{1}{2}$
a hyperbola with centre $\left(0, \frac{1}{2}\right),$ transverse axis 1 and conjugate axis $\frac{1}{2}$

solution.text: Given equation of an ellipse is $$ x^{2}+4 y^{2}=4 $$ $\Rightarrow \quad \frac{x^{2}}{4}+\frac{y^{2}}{1}=1$ $\therefore$ Coordinate of positive end of minor axis is $B(0,1)$ Let mid-point of the chord $B P$ is $M(h, k)$ Then, $\quad(h, k)=\left(\frac{0+x}{2}, \frac{1+y}{2}\right)$ $\Rightarrow \quad h=\frac{x}{2} \quad \Rightarrow x=2 h$ and $\quad k=\frac{1+y}{2} \Rightarrow y=2 k-1$ $\therefore$ $P(x, y)=\{2 h,(2 k-1)\}$ Since, the point '$P$' lies ellipses so form Eq. (i). we get $(2 h)_{1}^{2}+4(2 k-1)^{2}=4$ $\Rightarrow \quad 4 h^{2}+4(2 k-1)^{2}=4$ $\Rightarrow \quad h^{2}+4 k^{2}+1-4 k=1$ $\Rightarrow \quad h^{2}+4 k^{2}-4 k=0$ Thus, required locus is an ellipse whose equation is $x^{2}+4 y^{2}-4 y=0$ $\Rightarrow \quad \frac{(x-0)^{2}}{1}+\frac{\left(y-\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}}{\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)}=1$ whose centre $\left(0, \frac{1}{2}\right)$ and major and minor axis $\frac{1}{2}$
